jobs.description:
Description

Job Summary: The Housing Navigator assists and supports the client in finding secure housing. Works as a liaison between the client and landlords or property management offices. Works with clients to develop and carry out action plans that improve their financial health to sustain housing. Maintains housing listing database.

Essential Functions

Conduct comprehensive assessments to determine clients' housing needs, preferences, and eligibility for various housing programs.Develop and implement individualized housing plans in collaboration with clients, focusing on their goals and barriers to housing stability.Provide ongoing case management, including regular check-ins, crisis intervention, and advocacy.Assist clients in identifying and applying for appropriate housing options, including private market rentals, subsidized housing, and transitional housing programs.Conduct housing search workshops and provide one-on-one support in navigating housing applications, tenant rights, and responsibilities.Accompany clients to housing viewings, interviews, and lease signings as needed.Build and maintain relationships with landlords, property managers, and housing providers to increase access to housing opportunities for clients.Mediate and negotiate with landlords on behalf of clients to address any issues that may arise before and after placement.Must be able to engage the family and yet maintain the boundaries of a helping relationship.Collaborate with community organizations, service providers, and local government agencies to coordinate resources and referrals for clients.Maintain accurate and up-to-date client records, including case notes, housing plans, and progress reports.Track and report on housing outcomes, including placements, retention rates, and barriers encountered.Ensure compliance with all relevant policies, procedures, and funding requirements.The position requires the ability to meet with children/families in various locations in the community. The positions require flexibility to work varied hours including some evenings and weekends.Must perform other duties as assigned by the program Director and/or President/Chief Executive Officer.

Education: High school diploma or equivalent with minimum of 12 units in Social Services or other related field or demonstrate knowledge through comparable work experience.

Skills: Must have strong communication skills, written and verbal; able to make good, logical independent decisions within guidelines, accept responsibility; be detailed oriented, dependable, and reliable, committed, highly motivated, and adaptable; have self-confidence, strong time management skills and a professional code of ethics and professional demeanor; and take pride in producing a high-quality product.

Experience

jobs.title: Program Coordinator – Family Housing
jobs.description:
Help Families Build Lasting Housing Stability

Homeward Bound of Marin is seeking a compassionate and organized Program Coordinator to support families at the Nuestra Casa program and Oma Village as they work toward housing stability, self-sufficiency, and personal goals.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Family Programs, you’ll provide comprehensive, housing-focused case management, coordinate CalAIM services, support program enrollment, and connect families with community resources. You’ll work closely with program staff, landlords, service providers, and community partners to help families maintain stable housing.

This is an opportunity for an experienced human-services professional who values Housing First, trauma-informed care, accountability, and compassionate service.

What You’ll Do

Maintain a caseload of up to 18 families and provide comprehensive, housing-focused case management servicesSupport family intake, assessment, eligibility determination, documentation, enrollment, and housing placementComplete CalAIM enrollments for eligible families and meet Enhanced Care Management and Community Supports requirementsCreate and maintain assessments, care plans, service records, and outcome documentation in HMIS and HIPPO (Salesforce)Ensure documentation is timely, accurate, billing-ready, and prepared for quality reviews and auditsServe as the primary Coordinated Entry contact for Nuestra Casa families and connect them with appropriate housing and resourcesWork with residents, landlords, housing communities, shelter programs, and community partners to support housing retentionHelp families address barriers, build life and money-management skills, and increase economic independenceProvide supportive counseling, referrals, crisis intervention, and strengths-based problem-solvingConduct habitability inspections and annual assessments of residents’ service needsHelp fill housing vacancies promptly by coordinating qualified referrals with Homeward Bound programs and local partnersPartner with program and volunteer managers to coordinate volunteer-led events for familiesParticipate in staff meetings, supervision, training, chart reviews, and other quality-assurance activitiesMaintain confidentiality and communicate with families, colleagues, and partners with respect, dignity, and kindness

You’ll also provide emergency support when needed, which may include coordinating with law enforcement, psychiatric services, community agencies, and other Homeward Bound staff.

Required

What We’re Looking For

Two to three years of experience working with under-resourced or low-income populationsExperience in residential or housing programs and knowledge of the Housing First modelKnowledge of life skills, money management, and tenant rights and responsibilities under fair housing lawsKnowledge of substance use and mental health issues that may affect housing stabilityStrong communication, organization, documentation, collaboration, and crisis-management skillsA valid driver’s license, current vehicle insurance, and the ability to drive approximately 250 miles per month between sites throughout Marin CountyAbility to travel between housing sites, use a computer for moderate periods, occasionally stoop, crouch, kneel, or crawl, and lift or move up to 40 pounds

Preferred

Bachelor’s degree in social work, social welfare, psychology, or a related field, or five years of comparable work experienceExperience supporting individuals or families experiencing homelessnessExperience with CalAIM, Enhanced Care Management, Community Supports, HMIS, or Salesforce

Why Join Homeward Bound?

At Homeward Bound, our employees make a tangible difference every day. We believe supporting our team is essential to supporting our community.

We Offer

100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance403(b) retirement plan with discretionary employer matchThree weeks of paid vacation annuallyEmployee Assistance ProgramComplimentary lunch at our administrative siteA collaborative, mission-driven workplace where your work has lasting impact

To Apply

Please send your résumé and cover letter to careers@hbofm.org and include Program Coordinator | Nuestra Casa Family Program in the subject line.

Make an Impact

Join a mission-driven team helping veterans and their families transition from homelessness to permanent housing. As a Housing Navigator, you will work directly with veterans to guide them through every step of the housing process, including housing search, landlord engagement, lease support, move-in coordination, and housing stability services.

This role is ideal for someone passionate about housing access, case management, outreach, and supportive services who wants to make a direct impact in the lives of veterans experiencing homelessness.

For Housing Navigators supporting HUD-VASH, SSVF, or county-funded housing programs:

Maintain knowledge of program eligibility, housing regulations, and supportive service requirementsCoordinate with VA programs, supportive housing initiatives, and local Continuum of Care systemsConduct street outreach and community engagement activities as assignedSupport coordinated entry, housing referrals, and care coordination across programs

Full-Time | In-Person. | Location: Huntington Beach & Laguna Hills, CA




About the Role

The Care Coordinator is the day-to-day link between clients, Caregivers, staffing, recruiting, and HR. The primary focus is keeping client schedules fully staffed, communicating changes quickly, and solving problems before they affect service. This role also supports recruiting, hiring, onboarding, orientation, employee relations, and basic HR documentation for Caregivers. Success requires strong follow-through, good judgment, comfort with difficult conversations, and the ability to shift priorities in a fast-paced home care environment.

    Reassignment Applicants: Eligible Reassignment clients should contact their Disability Counselor for assistance.

DESCRIPTIONThe Department of Medicine is responsible for fulfilling the teaching, research, and clinical missions of the University of California, San Diego and employs 486+ full-time salaried faculty members and 100+ academic appointees. Staff personnel include 600+ staff in 9 bargaining units, students, and volunteers. There are 250 clinical faculty practicing at multiple sites.

Under the general supervision of the social work supervisor, the Trans Health Project (THP) Case Manager provides comprehensive, trauma-informed, gender-affirming, and culturally responsive case management support services to Black and Latina transgender women, prioritizing participants enrolled in the THP initiative research project with UCSD. This position supports Black and Latina transgender women experiencing barriers to health care, HIV prevention and treatment services, housing stability, economic security, behavioral health services, and other social determinants of health.

Using a participant-centered and strengths-based approach, the THP Case Manager assists participants in identifying goals, advocating for their needs across systems of care, accessing gender-affirming services, and addressing barriers to overall health and well-being. The position provides care coordination, resource linkage, and service advocacy, while working collaboratively with community partners and research collaborators to support participant engagement, retention, and connection to services, while ensuring confidentiality and compliance with organizational, funder, and research requirements. The ideal candidate possesses experience working with transgender and BIPOC communities, demonstrates cultural humility and responsiveness, and has knowledge of the unique challenges impacting Black and Latina transgender women. Spanish-language proficiency is strongly preferred.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSPossession of a bachelor's degree in social work from a program approved by the Council on Social Work Education, and one year of experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience; and knowledges and abilities essential to the successful performance of the duties assigned to the position.

Computer/Office Equipment Skills: Must be comfortable working in PC/Windows-based environments. Must be proficient with Microsoft Office.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks with shifting priorities.

Experience working with the LGBTQ community and persons living with or affected by HIV infection, particularly young Latina and Black transgender women, in San Diego County.

Homeward Bound of Marin is seeking a compassionate and organized Program Coordinator to support families at the Nuestra Casa program and Oma Village as they work toward housing stability, self-sufficiency, and personal goals.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Family Programs, you’ll provide comprehensive, housing-focused case management, coordinate CalAIM services, support program enrollment, and connect families with community resources. You’ll work closely with program staff, landlords, service providers, and community partners to help families maintain stable housing.

This is an opportunity for an experienced human-services professional who values Housing First, trauma-informed care, accountability, and compassionate service.

You’ll also provide emergency support when needed, which may include coordinating with law enforcement, psychiatric services, community agencies, and other Homeward Bound staff.

Required
